canonical_name: AI Startup Studio (Yapay Zeka Startup Studio)
aliases: Yapay Zeka Yıldızları AI Startup Studio
organizer: Vodafone Türkiye Vakfı (Vodafone Turkey Foundation) & Habitat Derneği (Habitat Association)
eligibility_verbatim: Per Anadolu Ajansı (Turkey's state news agency) reporting on the program: high school students aged 14-18 nationwide could apply individually or as a team ('bireysel ya da takım olarak'); the 2025-26 cohort received 119 applications and selected 25 young entrepreneurs. Habitat Derneği's own official page confirms the program, its partners, and an application deadline, but the exact eligibility-criteria sentence could not be directly fetched/quoted from the primary application page (blocked, see notes).
eligible_grades: Turkish high school (lise), all grades — nationwide open call, individual or team application
turkey_access_reasoning: This is a Turkey-domestic program organized by Turkish entities specifically for Turkish high schoolers ('Türkiye genelindeki tüm lise öğrencileri'), so eligibility for a Turkey-based student is inherently the design intent. Held at ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONDITIONS rather than VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE only because the precise eligibility sentence could not be directly fetched/quoted from the organizer's own primary application page (persistent 403 block across multiple attempts) — evidence instead comes from a co-organizer's official domain (habitatdernegi.org, confirms existence/partners/deadline) plus national press-agency reporting (age range and mechanics).
international_access_notes: Program is designed for students in Turkey; not framed as open to non-Turkey-resident students. No explicit citizenship requirement found (residency/school-location in Turkey appears to be the operative criterion).
team_or_national_delegation_required: No — individual or self-formed team application, not a national delegation
current_cycle_label: Most recent cohort completed 2026-02-18 (application deadline for that cohort was 2025-10-29); next cycle not yet announced as of this research date
cost_notes: Free to participate. The program itself awards cash prizes functioning as seed funding — the 2025-26 cohort's winning team ('Mergen', an AI-powered personalized study-plan platform) received a 100,000 TL prize.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Başvurular için yeni son tarih: 29 Ekim 2025 Saat:23.59. Partners: Vodafone Vakfı (Vodafone Foundation) and Habitat Derneği (Habitat Association). Application via JotForm / yapayzekayildizlari.org/ai-startup-studio.

High school students aged 14-18; three-month program with 16 training sessions and 2 networking meetings; mentoring via Vodafone Volunteers; 119 applications, 25 participants in final cohort; winning project 'Mergen' received 100,000 TL; program completed as of 2026-02-18; parent initiative 'Yapay Zeka Yıldızları' has reached 98,000+ students across Turkey's 81 provinces.

notes_uncertainties: Directly fetching the official application page (yapayzekayildizlari.org/ai-startup-studio) failed with HTTP 403 on every attempt (tried https, http, and www/non-www variants), so the age range (14-18) and mechanics (individual/team, 119 applicants, 25 selected) are sourced from a WebFetch-summarized Anadolu Ajansı press article rather than a raw quote I fetched myself — flagged per evidence rule. The co-organizer's own domain (habitatdernegi.org) WAS directly fetched and confirms the program is real, names both partners, and gives a concrete past deadline, which anchors this as a genuine, currently-operating program rather than a rumor. This record satisfies BOTH target #1 (a genuine Turkish corporate-foundation program with real selection, real mentorship, and explicit 14-18 high-school-age eligibility — the first one found across 5 corporate foundations checked in this pass) and, partially, target #2 (it has a real cash-prize/seed-funding component, though structured as a single end-of-cohort prize to the winning team rather than an ongoing per-individual grant). Recommend a second reviewer attempt the official page via a browser (not our WebFetch tool) to upgrade this to VERIFIED and pin down the exact verbatim eligibility sentence.

canonical_name: The Pollination Project — Daily Seed Grant
eligibility_verbatim: We accept applications from individuals, groups, and startup not-for-profit organizations based anywhere in the world as long as the work is volunteer-led. [...] Your group or organization must not have paid staff. [...] You must have started some level of work on your project.
eligible_grades: Not education-level gated; no age floor found on either official page checked
turkey_access_reasoning: Primary source explicitly confirms worldwide eligibility ('based anywhere in the world') with no age floor found across two official pages (funding-eligibility and apply). Held at ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONDITIONS rather than VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE because there is no explicit statement that minors specifically are eligible (this is an absence of a restriction, not an explicit confirmation of inclusion), and because the requirement to 'receive a wire transfer or Paypal payment in US dollars' creates practical friction for a student under 18 who may not hold their own bank/PayPal account — likely needs a parent/guardian to receive the funds.
international_access_notes: Explicitly worldwide; no country exclusions found on either official page fetched.
team_or_national_delegation_required: No — individuals or informal, volunteer-led groups are both eligible
current_cycle_label: Rolling/ongoing — applications accepted and reviewed monthly year-round
cost_notes: Free to apply; the grant itself provides up to $500 USD to the applicant's project, one grant per person/group/project lifetime.

evidence.raw_excerpt: We accept applications from individuals, groups, and startup not-for-profit organizations based anywhere in the world as long as the work is volunteer-led. Your group or organization must not have paid staff. You or your organization must be able to receive a wire transfer. Annual budget must be less than $50,000, and the total cost for the project must be less than $10,000.

We welcome applications on a rolling basis. Applications which are received in full before the final day of the month will be reviewed by our team during the following month and decisions will be shared with all applicants at the end of that month. Maximum one seed grant of up to $500 per person/group/project lifetime. You must have started some level of work on your project.

notes_uncertainties: This directly answers target #2: a genuine ONGOING (rolling, not one-time-competition) micro-grant program open worldwide to individuals for social/environmental projects, with no institutional gatekeeping and no age floor found. Two independent official pages were directly fetched and quoted, so the program's existence and mechanics are marked VERIFIED. turkey_student_access is nonetheless held at ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONDITIONS (not VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE) because minors are never explicitly named as eligible or ineligible — this is a genuine silence in the source, not a confirmed inclusion, consistent with the mission's capping rule. Recommend the next reviewer treat 'must have already started work on your project' as the key practical bar (this is not a grant for an idea alone) and flag the PayPal/wire-transfer step as needing adult assistance for a Turkey-based minor.

canonical_name: UN Major Group for Children and Youth (MGCY)
aliases: Major Group for Children and Youth
organizer: UN Major Group for Children and Youth (self-organized, UN DESA-recognized major group under the UN sustainable development process)
host_institution: Recognized major group under UN DESA / UN Sustainable Development framework
eligibility_verbatim: If you are a young person age 30 and below, and do not belong to or formally represent a youth led, child led, youth serving or child serving entity you can engage in the UN by becoming a member of the legal entity of the UNMGCY.
eligible_grades: Not education-gated; age-gated only (30 and under)
turkey_access_reasoning: No country restriction found on the official 'Get Involved' page (directly fetched and quoted); individual online registration, no fee. Held at ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONDITIONS because: (1) no explicit minimum age is stated, so it is unconfirmed whether a 16-17-year-old is treated identically to an 18+ member in practice; (2) MGCY's substantive work centers on formal UN processes (HLPF, ECOSOC Youth Forum) where in-person accreditation at UN venues commonly defaults to 18+ in practice — the adjacent body YOUNGO (UNFCCC youth constituency) states 'Representatives shall normally be at least 18 years of age. Younger representatives may be registered at the discretion of the secretariat,' and MGCY likely follows a similar informal norm even though its own page does not say so explicitly.
international_access_notes: No country restriction found; open worldwide via an online registration form.
cost_notes: No membership fee found on official pages reviewed.

evidence.raw_excerpt: If you are a young person age 30 and below... you can engage in the UN by becoming a member of the legal entity of the UNMGCY. All members must adhere to the Process and Procedures of the MGCY and agree with the values and principles of the MGCY: solidarity, diversity, justice, equity, universality, inclusion, human rights, and the integrity of the planet.

Mandated, formal, and self-organised space for children and youth (under 30) to contribute to and engage in UN policy processes, including the High-Level Political Forum (HLPF) and ECOSOC Youth Forum, working through Constituencies/Working Groups.

notes_uncertainties: Directly answers target #4: a genuine, individually-joinable, UN-recognized youth advisory body distinct from UNICEF Voices of Youth (already CANDIDATE from Wave 1). Kept at CANDIDATE rather than upgraded further because practical substance for a 16-17-year-old specifically (versus a college-age member) is unconfirmed — likely starts as remote working-group/mailing-list engagement, with in-person UN session representation realistically gated to 18+ by informal convention. Recommend the next reviewer treat this as 'genuinely accessible for remote engagement, uncertain for in-person UN representation as a minor' rather than a full parity claim with older members.

aliases: KidsRights Action Developer / Fund Catcher / Dreaming Big
eligibility_verbatim: for everyone from 12 up to 24 years old that wants to contribute to a lasting change for children's rights in their communities and beyond. [...] When you hand in your project plan, we will make a decision whether you will be eligible as an Action Developer or Fund Catcher.
eligible_grades: Not school-gated; age-gated. Note: a related KidsRights page uses '12 to 29' for the broader 'State of Youth' branding — see notes_uncertainties for this inconsistency.
turkey_access_reasoning: The age range (12-24) comfortably includes Turkish high schoolers, and the program is described as open to contributors 'in their communities and beyond' without a hard country allowlist in what was found. However, the confirmed 'State of Youth Chapters' identified in research (Brazil, Kenya, India in the pilot; Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe, Malawi in later coverage) do not include Turkey. It is unconfirmed whether an individual can submit a project plan (Action Developer / Fund Catcher tiers) without their country already having an established Chapter, or whether Turkey-based applicants can register directly outside that structure.
international_access_notes: Framed as global/community-based rather than a fixed country list, but no explicit Turkey confirmation found, and named chapters so far are concentrated in the Global South (Africa, South Asia, Latin America).
team_or_national_delegation_required: No — individual project-plan submission ('hand in your project plan')
current_cycle_label: Ongoing/rolling program with staged levels: Action Developer -> Fund Catcher -> Dreaming Big
cost_notes: Free to apply. Fund Catcher level provides 'a small fund' to improve/expand a project (reported elsewhere as up to EUR 500 depending on country); Dreaming Big level provides support to start or expand a youth organization.

evidence.raw_excerpt: for everyone from 12 up to 24 years old that wants to contribute to a lasting change for children's rights in their communities and beyond... When you hand in your project plan, we will make a decision whether you will be eligible as an Action Developer or Fund Catcher... Even though you will first be accepted as an Action Developer, you will still get the chance to apply for the Fund Catcher level once you are finished.
State of Youth empowers young people aged 12 to 29... Pilot Program during the summer, in which it gained its first 9 Chapters, from 3 different countries: Brazil, Kenya, and India.

notes_uncertainties: Directly relevant to targets #2 and #3: this is a genuine ongoing, individually-applied, staged funding program (not the annual, nomination-only International Children's Peace Prize, which Wave 1 already has on file) — but it is distinct from, not the same as, a 'fellowship for past Prize winners/alumni' that target #3 asked about (see closeout for that distinction). IMPORTANT TOOLING CAVEAT: thekidsrightschangemakers.org could not be directly fetched — three separate attempts across two different pages on that domain all failed with 'read ECONNRESET' (a connection-level reset, not a 403/404), which looks like a transient hosting/TLS issue rather than a deliberate bot block. Evidence here is therefore built from search-engine-indexed snippets of that exact official domain (medium confidence), not a tool-fetched direct quote — flagged per the evidence rule. A second reviewer should re-attempt this domain (ideally via browser) to upgrade to VERIFIED, confirm the 12-24 vs 12-29 age inconsistency, and directly confirm whether Turkey-based applicants without an existing 'Chapter' can still submit an individual project plan.
